research_profile.summary_bio: Shama Abidi (MPhil in Pharmacy Practice, Department of Pharmacy Practice, Faculty of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, University of Karachi, Karachi, Pakistan) is a Senior Pharmacist / Clinical Pharmacist at Department of Pharmacy Services, Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi, Pakistan. Her verified research portfolio spans 5 peer-reviewed publications and conference abstracts in the Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (PJPS) and Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (JPPP), focusing on ICU carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship (N=134, 87.3% physician acceptance), antianginal pharmacotherapy outcomes (N=110, SAQ-7 & Naranjo ADR assessment), high-alert medication safety (N=60), and AI vs. clinical pharmacist interventions.

research_documents.extracted_text:
Title: Evaluating knowledge of high-alert medications among nurses, pharmacists, and clinicians to improve medication safety
Authors: Fatima Baig, Aqsa Bilekhia, Shama Abidi, Safia Ahmed
Journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 223, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, pp. 146-147)
DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2485639
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi
Sample Size: N = 60 healthcare professionals (20 clinicians, 20 nurses, 20 pharmacists) + 6-month HAM consumption audit
Key Evidence Summary: Assessed hospital staff knowledge and 6-month consumption patterns (June-Nov 2024) of High-Alert Medications (HAMs), specifically electrolytes. Pharmacists achieved the highest knowledge score (80%), followed by nurses (75%) and clinicians (70%), identifying targeted gaps in drug compatibility, storage, and labeling.

research_documents.authors_json: ["Fatima Baig", "Haris Aziz Siddiqui", "Aqsa Bilekhia", "Shama Abidi", "Safia Ahmed"]
research_documents.journal_or_venue: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 225, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, p. 149)
research_documents.extracted_text:
Title: AI meets human expertise: Comparision between clinical pharmacist interventions and artificial intelligence at a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan
Authors: Fatima Baig, Haris Aziz Siddiqui, Aqsa Bilekhia, Shama Abidi, Safia Ahmed
Journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 225, PESP Conference 2025 Part A) (Vol. 18, No. S2, 2485639, p. 149)
DOI: 10.1080/20523211.2025.2485639
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi
Sample Size: N = 60 patients over 6 months (June - November 2024)
Key Evidence Summary: Prospective study comparing clinical pharmacist interventions with AI (ChatGPT 4.0) across drug-drug interactions, renal-adjusted antibiotic dosing, and electrolyte imbalance management. Validated by 3 independent clinical pharmacists; demonstrated that while AI detected DDIs and electrolyte issues, human clinical pharmacists were indispensable for accurate renal-adjusted antibiotic dosing in ICU settings.

Title: Effectiveness and safety assessment of calcium channel blockers compared to beta blockers in patients with angina: An observational study
Authors: Shama Abidi (First Author), Saira Saeed Khan, Sadaf Naeem, Humera Siddiqui, Sumaira Khadim, Saima Saleem, Saira Erum Ejaz, Syed Ishtiaq Rasool, Syeda Maheen Zahidi
Journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 37, No. 3, May 2024, pp. 639-649)
DOI: 10.36721/PJPS.2024.37.3.REG.639-649.1
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: IBC KU-317/2023 (Institutional Bio-ethical Research Committee, University of Karachi)
Sample Size: N = 110 angina patients (61 male, 49 female; June 2022 - June 2023)
Key Evidence Summary: Evaluated Beta Blockers (BB, 36.36%), Calcium Channel Blockers (CCB, 54.4%), and CCB+BB combination (9.8%) in tertiary care cardiology OPDs using Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) and Naranjo ADR scale. Improved angina symptoms in 83/110 patients (p < 0.05). CCB SAQ-7 score (83.97 ± 3.18) and combination (82.64 ± 5.12) outperformed BB (80.46 ± 5.99), with CCB exhibiting fewer Definite/Probable ADRs over long-term angina control.

research_documents.title: Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study
research_documents.authors_json: ["Fizzah Ali", "Tabassum Zehra", "Nazir Ahmed Solangi", "Karim Ullah Makki", "Haris Aziz Siddiqui", "Shama Abidi"]
research_documents.journal_or_venue: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 35, No. 6, November 2022, pp. 1595-1601)
research_documents.extracted_text:
Title: Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study
Authors: Fizzah Ali, Tabassum Zehra, Nazir Ahmed Solangi, Karim Ullah Makki, Haris Aziz Siddiqui, Shama Abidi
Journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.) (Vol. 35, No. 6, November 2022, pp. 1595-1601)
DOI: 10.36721/PJPS.2022.35.6.REG.1595-1601.1
Study Site: Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College, Karachi
Ethics Approval: App#0592-2020 LNH-ERC (Liaquat National Hospital Ethical Committee)
Sample Size: N = 134 non-adherent carbapenem prescriptions in Medical ICU/HDU (Dec 2020 - May 2021)
Key Evidence Summary: Prospective interventional study at Liaquat National Hospital evaluating physician acceptance and clinical outcomes of pharmacist-led Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) interventions for carbapenem therapy. ASP interventions were accepted in 117/134 (87.3%) patients, resulting in 7-day clinical improvement in 99 (84.6%) patients and a significant reduction in 30-day readmission due to re-infection (p = 0.036). Interventions included renal dose adjustment for creatinine clearance (62.7%, n=84) and antibiotic de-escalation (25.4%, n=34).

email_drafts.subject: Prospective PhD Inquiry: Antimicrobial Stewardship & Intensive Care Pharmacotherapy — Dr. Shama Abidi (PharmD, MPhil)
email_drafts.body_text:
Dear Prof. Dr. Günther Fink,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to express my strong interest in pursuing a PhD under your supervision in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy & Pharmaceutical Sciences at Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute (Switzerland).

I recently studied your 2023 publication, "Association Between Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs and Antibiotic Use Globally" (DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.53806), which strongly aligns with my clinical research experience.

My prospective interventional research at Liaquat National Hospital evaluated a multidisciplinary carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program across medical/surgical ICUs (N=134, published in PJPS, 2022). That study demonstrated an 87.3% physician intervention acceptance rate and achieved 62.7% renal dose adjustments based on calculated creatinine clearance (p=0.036). Connecting this with your work on "Association Between Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs and Antibiotic Use Globally", I am eager to investigate clinical pharmacist-led stewardship models, therapeutic drug monitoring, and precision dosing for resistant pathogens.

Candidate Academic Summary:
• Senior Pharmacist, Liaquat National Hospital (18+ yrs tertiary care experience)
• MPhil in Pharmacy Practice, University of Karachi (Supervisor: Dr. Saira Saeed Khan)
• Peer-Reviewed Publications: PJPS (2020, 2022, 2024), JPPP (2025), FIP Montreal (2026)
• Vice President, Pakistan Pharmacist Association (PPA) Sindh Cabinet

I would be very grateful to learn whether your lab has supervision capacity for a prospective PhD candidate, and whether university or international doctoral fellowship tracks (e.g., graduate research/teaching assistantships) might be applicable.

Curriculum Vitae & Verified Credentials (Attached & Online):
• Complete Academic CV (PDF): https://shamaabidiphd.sbs/data/documents/Dr_Shama_Abidi_Academic_CV_2026.pdf
• Official ORCID Record: https://orcid.org/0009-0008-3714-1675
• LinkedIn Profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/shama-abidi-5a41a0304/

I have also attached my Academic CV to this email for your immediate review. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss a brief PhD research concept note or schedule a brief virtual meeting at your convenience.

Warm regards,
Dr. Shama Abidi, PharmD, MPhil (Pharmacy Practice)
Senior Clinical Pharmacist, Liaquat National Hospital & Medical College
Vice President, Pakistan Pharmacist Association (PPA) Sindh Cabinet
Email: shamaabidiphd@gmail.com | WhatsApp: +92 300 2460474
ORCID: 0009-0008-3714-1675 | LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/shama-abidi-5a41a0304/

Dear Prof. Dr. Siwei Wang,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to express my strong interest in pursuing a PhD under your supervision in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy & Pharmaceutical Sciences at Wenzhou Medical University (China).

I recently studied your 2024 publication, "Treatment of infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii" (DOI: 10.3389/fcimb.2024.1395260), which strongly aligns with my clinical research experience.

My prospective interventional research at Liaquat National Hospital evaluated a multidisciplinary carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program across medical/surgical ICUs (N=134, published in PJPS, 2022). That study demonstrated an 87.3% physician intervention acceptance rate and achieved 62.7% renal dose adjustments based on calculated creatinine clearance (p=0.036). Connecting this with your work on "Treatment of infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii", I am eager to investigate clinical pharmacist-led stewardship models, therapeutic drug monitoring, and precision dosing for resistant pathogens.

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to express my strong interest in pursuing a PhD under your supervision in the Department of Clinical Pharmacy & Pharmaceutical Sciences at Catharina Ziekenhuis (Netherlands).

I recently studied your 2023 publication, "Design and rationale of the efficacy of spinal cord stimulation in patients with refractory angina pectoris (SCRAP) trial" (DOI: 10.1002/clc.24016), which strongly aligns with my clinical research experience.

For my MPhil in Pharmacy Practice at the University of Karachi (supervised by Dr. Saira Saeed Khan), my thesis investigated the comparative effectiveness and safety of calcium channel blockers versus beta blockers in angina pectoris (N=110, PJPS 2024).
